items.detail: The **S&P 500** rose 0.3% to 7,744.06 Thursday, but the Nasdaq barely moved, up 0.1% to 26,713.03, as the Dow jumped 1.1%.
items.why: Investors sold tech and bought defensive stocks as Treasury yields fell and worries about AI debt eased.

items.detail: September producer prices rose **6.3%** from a year earlier, and their 1.3% monthly jump was the biggest since March 2022.
items.why: Energy drove most of the jump, with gasoline up 20.3% in the month on Iran-war oil prices.

items.detail: Even after the hot report, the 10-year Treasury yield fell about 14 basis points to roughly **5.05%** Thursday.
items.why: Traders cut bets on an October Fed hike and moved money from tech stocks into bonds.

items.detail: Indonesian stocks fell as much as **11.4%** Friday, their worst day since 1998, while the Kospi rebounded about 3%.
items.why: MSCI proposed cutting Indonesia to 'standalone' status, which could force about $3 billion of passive fund selling.

items.detail: The **Sensex** jumped 1,534 points to 74,315.61 Thursday, and the Nifty closed near 22,997, led by IT stocks.
items.why: Crude oil fell about 2%, which eases India's import bill and inflation pressure.

items.detail: The US **Russell 2000** gained about **1.4%** Thursday, a bounce one day after it entered a correction.
items.why: Lower Treasury yields eased borrowing costs for small companies, and money moved out of chipmakers.

items.detail: **Bitcoin** briefly fell to about $80,000, then held there and bounced back to roughly **$82,300** Friday morning.
items.why: Hot inflation data caused the dip, but buyers stepped in at the $80,000 support level.

items.detail: **Ether** recovered to about **$2,440** Friday after dipping near $2,380, but it is still below $2,500.
items.why: US spot ether ETFs had a second straight day of outflows Thursday, led by BlackRock's ETHA.

items.detail: **Solana** slipped to about **$102**, close to the $100 level, five days before its Alpenglow upgrade goes live.
items.why: Continued outflows from Solana ETFs are outweighing hopes for the October 21 upgrade.

items.detail: **Gold** rose 1.24% to $4,175.90 Thursday, snapping a three-day losing streak, and Comex futures neared **$4,200** Friday.
items.why: Hot producer prices drew buyers looking to hedge inflation, while a weaker dollar and lower yields helped.

crossCuttingTheme: Producer inflation hit 6.3%, but yields fell anyway as money left AI and chip stocks for bonds, defensive stocks and gold, which lifted the Dow, small caps and bullion while the Nasdaq stalled.
